monitor.telecom.hourlyNote: Hourly average of complete measurements only; hatched when an hour has none

monitor.telecom.bandLegend: Light band = IPv4 suggested normal range

monitor.telecom.risNote: Prefix visibility and withdrawal ratio need tracked prefixes to be configured; none are set, so they are not listed.
monitor.telecom.sourceNote: Atlas and RIS both belong to RIPE NCC and count as one source group; 100% ping or 0 origin changes alone do not imply normal.
monitor.telecom.howto1: IPv6 is normally about 85–90%, not 100%: a few Taiwan probes have no IPv6 themselves.
monitor.telecom.howto2: The 24-hour line averages only complete measurements (enough probes) into one point per hour; an hour with none is hatched. Until collection is fixed, long hatched stretches mean incomplete measurements, not a network problem.
monitor.telecom.howto3: A single dip is not an anomaly; worth attention only when it lasts 15+ minutes and IPv4 / IPv6 or success / reporting rates drop together.
monitor.telecom.howto4: This card pings a single target (K-root) from a single source (RIPE); to judge whether Taiwan is offline, compare with IODA or Cloudflare Radar.
monitor.telecom.howtoRef: References: RIPE Atlas docs, RIPE RIS docs, IODA, Cloudflare Radar developer docs
monitor.telecom.legacyHeader: RIPE NCC network observation · NETWORK OBSERVATION
monitor.telecom.descError: This update failed; the last successful measurements are kept, but a successful transfer or old data does not equal {current}.
monitor.telecom.descOk: Continuously observing RIPE Atlas end-to-end measurements and RIPE RIS BGP routing updates. Values are shown as-is; anomaly interpretation will be added once a baseline accumulates.
monitor.telecom.legacyFootnote: Atlas and RIS both belong to RIPE NCC and count as one source group. {current} only means at least one measurement is fresh; 100% ping, 0 origin changes or 0 withdrawals alone do not imply normal. Chart gaps stay blank and are not filled with 0.
